subject: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start
parts:
I have tried to extend the skeleton rstan package example to include a test, but could not get it to start the test. See below for details.

The zipped project is included, and it is also on https://github.com/dmenne/teststan

---

The package starts from the skeleton produces by packages rstan. Some additions were taken from the thread on
gfpca . A simple test case was added.

The package compiles successfully under RStudio and Windows 7, 64 bit Windows, rstan 2.9.0-3. Both 64 and 32 bit R was tested. Modules.cpp, Modules.o, teststan.dll and include\models.hpp were created.

When the test is started, it errors with

Error in Rcpp::loadRcppModules() :
  loadRcppModules can only be used within a .onLoad function
 
----

It would be nice if the skeleton would add a simple test case that runs. For examples, it is not immediately evident that a stan module `test1.stan` becomes `stan_fit4test1_mod` in DESCRIPTION, and it would help to see a sample case.


Dieter

messages.subject: Re: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start
parts:
Thanks for testing. I have added some minor correction in the revised project zip and also updated it on github.

To summarize:
  • Everything ok under Linux and Windows if the R CMD/rcmd toolchain is used.
  • Both under Linux and Windows the RStudio/devtools chain cannot be used because of the issue reported May 2015 on https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/828 and confirmed in September 2015 as a rcpp issue.
  • It would be nice if the skeleton could produce a self-contained project with a simple file and tests. Up to then, you can use https://github.com/dmenne/teststan

The cleanup and cleanup.win files need to be marked as executable

chmod +x cleanup*

and pushed to github. There's about 1000 tests in rstanarm that people could look at for inspiration. I suppose rstan.package.skeleton could come with a test, but I don't know what would be a meaningful test without any knowledge of what the package is for. A test could call sampling() on each of the elements of the stanmodel list, but how would it know what data are needed?

messages.subject: Re: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start
parts: I agree that I would not have had any problems if I had taken seriously that devtools/rcpp was the problem, not my settings in DESCRIPTION etc.
There's about 1000 tests in rstanarm that people could look at for inspiration.
rstanarm is an impressive package, but it's not something to use as a starter. And it is no about tests, but about settings.

I suppose rstan.package.skeleton could come with a test, but I don't know what would be a meaningful test without any knowledge of what the package is for. A test could call sampling() on each of the elements of the stanmodel list, but how would it know what data are needed?

Data needed: none. Or use 8schools.

 data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real y[N];
}

parameters {
  real mu;
}

model {
  mu ~ normal(0, 10);
  y ~ normal(mu, 1);
}

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start
parts:
Dirk Eddelbuettel replied on github: https://github.com/RcppCore/Rcpp/issues/468

  •  (RStudio or devtools)... "are local picks of your choosing... The only really relevant output is from R CMD"
  • On DE's suggestion, tried current master branch 0.12.4.5/2016-04-15 without change.
  • Shotgun `loadRcppModules` has been deprecated since January 2014. Use `loadModule("NameOfModuleClass", TRUE)` for loading instead
I have not been able to get a working version with `loadModule` yet, but I consider it a strong point.

messages.subject: Re: Adding test case to skeleton package: compile ok, test cannot start
parts:
With

Rcpp::loadModule("stan_fit4test1_mod", TRUE)

(replace with your module name)

in .zzz, the devtools chain works fine. Thanks to Dirk Eddelbuettel.

This should be changed in the skeleton.
